items.title: #7 chunking, hashing and block store
items.detail: Round-2 findings N1-N8 fixed, re-verified by me: 89 crate tests pass, fmt/clippy clean, scope clean, BlockId/ChunkRef untouched, CI green. Builder's evidence: 1800 simulated power-loss cases, 0 acked blocks lost, 0 wrong bytes, corrupt_synced reported after benign torn tail 271/1800 before, 0 after; 256 MiB pack opens in 1 ms with index, 227 ms full verified rebuild; header CRC added (format v2, 56-byte header, v1 refused); salvage(), verify_all(), acknowledge_corruption(), torn-tail sidecar, transactional roll, SYNCED base; 50 mutants 48 killed (2 equivalent); builds on Rust 1.89. Open: possible 25-35% single-thread slowdown (ingest 287 to 191 MiB/s, verified read 771 to 521) on the one clean pass, inconclusive on noisy passes; N9 cold-cache verify-on-dedup cost not measurable; sealed-pack cut at a record boundary only noticed via index checkpoint; default test time 2:17. Round-3 critic running a proper A/B of the old and new code, crash-during-recovery harness, and mutants on the new logic. | ROUND-3 VERDICT: NOT mergeable. F1 stale index.cix plus reused pack id loses acked blocks (2 of 6 after acknowledge_corruption then put, sync, crash); F2 whole-pack ACKED entry hides later corruption; F3 zero-filled last pack header makes open fail closed; F4 in-place move-down not crash-atomic (double fault loses an acked block); F5 loss reported only once, then clean; F6 unbounded torn sidecars, unsynced, truncates even when the sidecar write fails; F7 forged valid-CRC headers drop valid blocks (attacker model); F8 new_pack collides with next roll (GC). Held up: 4000 crash cases 0 acked lost, 0 wrong bytes; 180 s stress clean; header CRC; compat with core and meta. A/B: no performance regression (instructions equal within 0.3%, earlier 25-35% slowdown was load noise). 7 of 12 new mutants survived. Builder fixing with pack-id high-water, content-bound ACKED, copy-then-swap recovery, persistent loss marker.

items.title: #11 Linux FUSE mount
items.detail: Critic findings fixed, re-verified by me at 98c0f24: 43 unit tests on Mac, and in the Linux VM 46 unit + 39 mount + 5 regress tests pass, no mounts left. Defaults now safe: ttl 1 s, keep_cache off, opt-in SoleWriter with an Invalidator; Vfs panics become EIO then a clean unmount; keyed-lane worker pool (slow read no longer delays stat: 856 ms to 0.2 ms, builder's n=1); signal cleanup and stale-mount sweep; inode-reuse paranoid mode. Decisions for lead: cross-adapter permission policy (FUSE denies later O_WRONLY on a 0444 file, NFS allows), SoleWriter wiring by core/control plane (invalidate from outside Vfs calls), add 'Ino never reused' text to architecture doc (done on v1/vfs-trait), add a Linux mount CI job (command in report). 2 survivors: one equivalent, one control.

items.detail: Reply-cache connection bug FIXED and re-verified by me at 5122ff1 (110 crate tests, 5 new dupcache tests, ignored mount suite 17/17, no mounts left, CI green). Round-2 critic verdict: NOT mergeable with Translate as default. F1 ._x created before x exists (unzip exits 50, tarfile and ditto fail, git clone with tracked ._ files leaves a broken index; Hide and Store succeed); F2 a write to a real ._x file is accepted then lost after restart; F3 more than ~150 xattrs on a file make all its xattrs invisible (fix patch provided). Also: sidecar handles do not go stale on inode reuse, concurrent sidecar writes lose chunks, silent connections fill the cap, one-shot MNT can be raced by a polling attacker, SIGKILL of the host hangs ls/touch, inline_metadata stalls the server with a blocking Vfs, RPC claim not reproduced (14.3 to 13.4, not 19 to 13), 14 of 24 new-code mutants killed. Held up: SETATTR guard correct, reference balance 0 leaks in all 3 modes, handle MAC sound, RSS bounded (3-24 MiB), SIGTERM cleanup 66/66. Builder switching default to Hide first, then fixing Translate.

items.title: #26 cowfs-core: Vfs over store and meta
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. F1 deadlock: ensure_file holds the node write lock then takes the meta read lock while commit holds meta write then node read (repro hangs; builder's stress/kill9 never hit it). F2 promote_base removes base then forks: a failed fork loses base. F3 one corrupt block wedges the whole snapshot (fsync, readdir, fork, merkle_root all return Corrupt; other files' acked data lost at reopen) and a partial overwrite inside a corrupt chunk succeeds. Also: virtual inos reused across restart (wrong bytes), snapshot names accept .git/newline/ESC and case/NFC duplicates unlike the CLI, readdir flushes unrelated dirty data (48 MiB, 179 ms), alias table unbounded (469 MB after 500k creates), zero-id hole refs look dangling to GC. Held up: durability ordering, fsx 20k ops vs model, 60 s of overlapping writers (0 torn), hook failure recovery, EIO on corrupt reads. Bench (load 11-15): seq read 1351 MiB/s (13.6x slower than APFS page cache), 4K read 21.6k/s, seq write+fsync 390 MiB/s, lookups faster than std::fs. Builder fixing and re-merging fixed store and meta.

items.title: #34 cowfs-vfs-path: run the suite on native filesystems and through mounts
items.detail: Suite run on APFS, btrfs, ext4, FUSE and NFS. Posix level (56 checks): 0 failures natively and through FUSE; NFS mount 10 (9 silly rename, 1 AppleDouble Translate hides ._ names). FUSE adapter: no bug. NFS adapter bug found: the reply cache ignores the connection, so a second connection's identical xid replays the first connection's reply and the call never runs (sent to the #12 builder). Suite level corrections sent to the #29 builder (torn reads on ext4/btrfs/tmpfs at 512/4096 B, statfs files=0 on btrfs, com.apple.* xattrs, atime-only ctime, xattr name prefix, LINK_MAX hang). Client-side, not adapter: sparse blocks, statfs caching, silly rename. 2 unexplained flakes. | CRITIC VERDICT: NOT mergeable. No root escape (28 adversarial tests, all *at-relative, O_NOFOLLOW, no fd leaks in 50k cycles; btrfs 54/0 and ext4 54/0 reproduced; full-level matrix reproduces exactly). Blockers: F1 name_removed uses st_nlink-1 so files with an unseen hardlink never reclaim (300/300 nodes live, +445 fds) and the next file reusing that (dev,ino) gets the OLD Ino; F8 `matches!(errno, Some(EACCES | EPERM | EROFS))` is a bitwise OR, so the read-only reopen retry never runs (0444 file write fails once the cache is cold); F9 cached directory listing misses files created outside PathVfs; F4 hardlink_pairs_8000 takes 46-122 s vs a 60 s timeout on APFS, so '0 Posix failures' flips with load. 8 of 13 mutants survive: the control is blind to inode lifecycle. Builder fixing, merging main and adopting the frozen trait.
